p.src:
The English bur[y]ing place is a green slope near the walls, under the pyramidal tomb of
Cestius, & is I think the most beautiful & solemn cemetery I ever beheld. To see the sun
shining on its bright grass fresh when we visited it with the autumnal dews, & hear the
whispering of the wind among the leaves of the trees which have overgrown the tomb of
Cestius, & the coil which is stirring in the sunwarm earth & to mark the tombs mostly
of women & young people who were buried there, one might, if one were to die, desire
the sleep they seem to sleep. Such is the human mind & so it peoples with its wishes
vacancy & oblivion.
 (L ii 59–60)
